title: Reviewer approval is a defined assertion that the Spell performs exactly the Executive Document's actions, with none omitted and none added
content:
A.1.10.2.4.9.2.8 draws the consequence of the authoring bans: "As the Reviewers are prohibited from modifying the contents of a Spell via commits or authoring, **the most important power they possess is whether to approve the progression of a Spell** to its next stage."

It then defines what approval asserts. A Reviewer approving the final deployed Spell for handover "represents confirmation that they believe... that the Spell has fulfilled the Spell Team's role of creating a smart contract that performs **the exact set of actions described in the Executive Document, with no actions omitted or additional actions present**."

The assertion is bidirectional, and both directions are load-bearing. Nothing missing is what most reviews check. Nothing extra is the security-critical half — the failure mode of a malicious Spell is not an absent action but a present one, and it is far harder to notice, since spotting an unexpected addition requires understanding all the code rather than ticking off a list.

The powerlessness and the power are connected. Because a Reviewer cannot fix what they find, approval cannot be a negotiated "good enough after my edits" — it is a clean claim about an artifact they had no hand in shaping. That is what makes it meaningful evidence rather than a co-author's self-assessment, and it is why the four authoring bans exist to protect it.

The language is also honest about its epistemic status: "confirmation that they believe." Approval is a sincere professional judgment, not a proof, which is why the framework layers further independent checks after it (the Governance Point's review, Ecosystem Spell Validation) rather than treating a signature as the end of verification.
description: A.1.10.2.4.9.2.8 identifies approval as the Reviewers' only power precisely because they cannot modify anything, and gives it a bidirectional completeness meaning.
